text:
Calgary held a 1-0 lead for 45 minutes on a power-play goal that was only a 6 percent chance, and Vancouver spent the third period making that scoreline look like a mistake. Matt Coronato's wrist shot at 14:51 of the first was the lone Flames goal, and it came while the Canucks were actually carrying slightly more of the early play than the score suggested. Calgary led the first period in chance quality, 0.71 expected goals to 0.53, but the game belonged to Vancouver from there.

The turn came in the second and became a rout in the third. The Canucks out-created the Flames 0.94 to 0.49 in the middle period, then 2.14 to 0.50 in the final one. Liam Ohgren tied it 1:28 into the third on a 39 percent chance, and Elias Pettersson put Vancouver ahead on a backhand at 9:04. Drew O'Connor made it 3-1 at 16:33, and Aatu Räty added an empty-looking finish 43 seconds later on a 79 percent look. Four goals in one period, all at even strength, and Calgary never had an answer.

The full-game numbers back up what the third period showed. Vancouver finished with 3.61 expected goals to Calgary's 1.70, and wins 71 percent of simulated replays of every shot. Shot attempts were dead even at 63 each, so this was about quality, not volume. Leevi Meriläinen stopped 23 of 24 and saved 0.7 goals more than expected, while Devin Cooley was roughly average behind a team that gave up too much in the slot. Tom Willander had two assists and Ohgren a goal and an assist.
